fixed.problem: W15B-01 (major, data loss): a Redo or a Try again on a task whose pull request is open reset the task's folder with `checkout -B` and dropped a commit the person had made there, without a word, and spent model calls. Two paths did it: resuming the branch as GitHub has it (a Tasks-row Redo with no merge card, a Try again), and redoing from main while the pull request keeps the branch name (a Redo that closed a merge card). Bench before: 4 specialist calls ran and the commit was gone.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts 'w15-tail, wave 15 run B: a Redo or a Try again never drops a commit made in the task's folder (W15B-01)' > '(a) the Tasks row's Redo of a done task with an open pull request, no merge card ...' and '(b) ... whose conflict notice is open (a redo from main) ...'; apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts 'w15-tail, wave 15 run B' > 'W15B-01: the Tasks row's Redo of a done task with a commit the person made in its folder holds it ...'. That case goes through POST /tasks/:id/action redo, a session, GET /inbox options, a daemon restart and the card's Try again; it failed on the base code with "expected 'done' to be 'needs_human'".
fixed.how: Before each of executeIn's two resets (pr-executor.ts), `personsCommitAtRisk(git, branch, base)` checks whether the reset would drop a commit of the person's. It looks at the local branch, and at HEAD when HEAD is on that branch or detached. These are not the person's: commits GitHub's branch or the base already has, Forerunner's own unpushed base merge and work-in-progress commits (as folderHold treats them), and Forerunner's own task commit whose push did not go through. That last one is named by the new RUN_UNPUSHED_REF, set from the commit until the push succeeds, in executeIn and in conflict(). Anything it cannot identify holds the run (fails closed). An unpushed rebuild is put back first (undoUnpushedRebuild). When held, the run ends before any model call with { outcome: 'needs_human', summary, costUsdMicro: 0, branch }, and the runner, unchanged, files the cannot-run card. The two sentences: HELD_FOR_COMMIT_RESUME and heldForCommitRedo(base). folderHold itself is unchanged. Uncommitted changes stay as built: cleanAfterCutShortRun sets them aside under failedRef and keeps them, without saying so. A sibling regression test checks that Forerunner's own commit whose push was refused still runs again on Try again (pre-receive hook on the fake GitHub); it passed before and after the fix.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check 3 (GitHub through the proxy; the hold itself makes no model call). (a) In a repository project, run a task to done so its PR waits for Merge. In its task folder (<data dir>/worktrees/<task id>; the Overview row's folder), add a file and run `git commit`, without pushing. Press Redo on the task's Tasks row, then Start session. Expect: the task's cost does not grow and the session log shows no run of it. The Tasks row reads 'Needs your decision: it could not run'. The Inbox card '"<task>" could not run' reads 'Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub: push it or undo it, then press Try again.' with Try again / Cancel task. `git log` in the folder still shows the commit, and the PR branch on GitHub is unchanged. Quit and reopen the app. Run `git push origin <branch>` in the folder and press Try again: a session runs the task from that branch, and the PR then contains your file. (b) With a '"<task>" conflicts with main' card open, press Redo on its Tasks row (the card is withdrawn), commit in the folder, and start a session. Expect the card body '… Its task folder has a commit that is not on GitHub, and doing the task again from main would drop it: undo it or keep it on another branch, then press Try again.' Undo it with `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` and press Try again: the task is done again from main. After w15-words merges (W15B-79), also read the session log's task line for the held task.

fixed.problem: W15B-02 (major, money): a removed project (one whose creation was undone) could still start work. A kept credential wait started its session by itself at every tick. Its handover schedule kept firing. POST /sessions and the chat started it. Its page offered Start session and Create a repository. A plan the intake was still drafting was filed after the Undo. And the creation's Undo went through while a session of the project ran. Bench before: POST /sessions on the removed project returned 202 and started a session.
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts 'w15-tail, wave 15 run B: a removed project starts nothing (W15B-02)': (a) Undo while the intake call is held, then no plan card, also after a restart (failed: a card was filed); (b) POST /sessions refused with one sentence and no session row, the chat's session.start refused, also after a restart (failed: 202 started); (c) a kept credential wait across a restart: the wake starts nothing and the wait leaves the key (failed: wake returned 1); (d) the handover schedule goes at the next tick, and starts from the handover job, budget_reset and message triggers are refused with no session row, also after a restart (failed: the schedule stayed); (e) the creation's Undo while a session runs is refused with its sentence, then goes through once the session ended (failed: undoable true). Also apps/ui/test/project.test.tsx 'w15-tail, wave 15 run B: a removed project's page (W15B-02)' (failed: no project-removed text).
fixed.how: One guard where every start passes: compose.ts startSession calls refuseRemovedProject after the local jobs and before the handover job and runSession. It throws ForerunnerError validation with removedProjectRefusal(project) (new in commands/project.ts): 'The project "<name>" was removed, so nothing of it runs.' HandoverJob's runSession checks too, because `fr jobs handover` bypasses startSession. Other paths: POST /sessions refuses before the scheduler is asked, so no session row is made. The chat's startBlocked port returns the same sentence. credentialWaits.wake takes a removed project's wait off its source, even while the credential still cannot serve, and starts nothing. refreshJobSchedules leaves archived projects out, so their handover schedule is removed. The intake refuses in propose after mustGet, and reads the status again right before it files the card; its background job records no failure for a removed project. project.create's new undoBlocked refuses while a session of the project is running, paused or planned (the intake's planning call and the chat's row don't count). ProjectPage says 'This project was removed.' instead of the status sentence and shows no Start session, Create a repository or plan banner. The fake daemon's POST /sessions refuses the same way (409 conflict, as the real daemon maps validation).
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check 3 (stand-in or live). 1) New project with a one-line brief, then at once Changes → Undo on 'Created the project … and made it the active project.' while 'Drafting the plan…' shows. After a minute the Inbox has no plan card for it. 2) Open the removed project (an old notification, or /projects/<id>): the header reads '<name> (removed)' and 'This project was removed.', with no Start session, no Create a repository and no plan banner. 3) In that project's chat say 'start a session': the answer is 'The project "<name>" was removed, so nothing of it runs.' and no session starts. 4) Start a session in a project made with New project, and while it runs open Changes: its creation row reads 'Cannot be undone now: a session of <name> is running. Stop it first.' After it ends, Undo works. 5) API key at its limit (bench-api --api-key limited): New project, add a task, Start (the wait is kept), Undo the creation. At the reset no session of it starts, and Settings shows no work waiting for the key.

fixed.problem: W15B-05 (minor, timers after stop): the null-mergeable re-read (W15-07) waited up to about 15 s per pull request, one PR after another, on a plain setTimeout that stop() did not cancel. After Quit a poll went on calling GitHub, and a main-branch move with N open PRs held one poll for N x 15 s.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/githost-watcher.test.ts 'w15-tail, wave 15 run B: the null-mergeable re-read (W15B-05)': with three PRs answering mergeable null, the poll still ran after 100 s of the injected clock (before the fix it needed 45 s of real time); stop() during a re-read left the poll running past the 10 s real-time limit.
fixed.how: Each poll gets a RereadBudget: the schedule's sum, 15 s by default, shared by all its PRs. The re-reads wait on deps.rereadClock (default SystemClock in real time; tests inject a SimulatedClock) with an AbortSignal. stop() aborts it. The poll then ends with that PR's cursor as it was and no baseline completed, and makes no further GitHub call: no default-branch heads, no merge retry, no deliveries.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check 3: with several open task PRs, merge one on GitHub so the others' mergeability is recomputed. The next poll's conflict notices arrive within about 15 s of the poll start, not 15 s per PR. Quit from the tray during a poll: the daemon log shows no GitHub request after the shutdown line.

fixed.how: A composed conversation test with a scripted chat model that obeys a questions card's quoted words. The card orders three things: widen the site rule, cancel the task 'Style the page', and raise the project budget to CHF 500. The model carries out one per turn (settings_set, task_transition, budget_set). Each turn ends in the read-back: pendingConfirmation names settings.set, task.transition or budget.set, actions are empty, and the site rule, budget and task are unchanged. Each request's system text carries the data rule. The gates that hold: a widening asks for a yes, a task change said in chat is read back, and a limit change the model asks for needs the person. No gate code was changed; agent.ts was not touched.

new_problems: The real daemon's onError overwrites `details.cause` with the error code, so POST /sessions on a removed project reaches the client as 409 'conflict' with details.cause 'validation', not 'project_removed' (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts app.onError). The message carries the sentence, so nothing breaks; the fake daemon was matched to 409 conflict.

Commands other than a start still act on a removed project when the chat names it by id or it is the active project: resolveProject (packages/commands/src/commands/shared.ts:56-58) returns an archived row by id, so for example task.create can add a task to it. No session or spend follows, because the start guard holds, but it is confusing. A later item could refuse every project-scoped command on an archived project.

folderHold (pr-executor.ts, the rebuild) still counts the folder's HEAD when HEAD is on another local branch, so a commit kept on another branch there holds the rebuild. personsCommitAtRisk does not count it. This is fail-closed, not data loss, but the two rules differ; the sentence '… keep it on another branch …' is true for the run and over-holds for the rebuild.

Edge case: if a person's commit was carried into a work-in-progress resume (checkout of the WIP branch) and the run's push then fails, RUN_UNPUSHED_REF marks a tip that includes the person's commit as Forerunner's own. A later 'Drop the branch' would then drop it as asked. This is rare; it only arises after an explicit drop.

The rebase-conflict card's 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch', answered after the person committed in the folder, is now held with the redo-from-main sentence (fail closed). The card's own explanation, 'The task is done again from main; a session starts for it.', does not mention this; it is w15-words' text to consider.

The cannot-run card's Try again explanation, 'Starts a session that tries again; first fix what stopped it (Edit changes who does it).', is shown under the W15B-01 hold too, where Edit is beside the point. Words for w15-words or run C.

The bench before-walk left a 'Create a repository for "Removed one (before) (removed)"?' card open. The session that ran on the removed project before the fix filed it. The guard now prevents this, but cards a removed project got before an upgrade stay open until withdrawn.
